summary: Chestnut Mountain lookout on Chestnut Ridge above Burke's Garden: 48-foot steel tower built 1929, removed circa 1980s; cabin rehabilitated 1994 as the Chestnut Knob AT shelter.

facts.status_note: Tower removed circa 1980s; the former lookout cabin, or a warden's house at the tower base, is now the Chestnut Knob AT shelter

access.note: Site lies on the Appalachian Trail, which runs over the top; no source we read says it is closed

visit.trail_note: From the Walker Gap parking area, hike southbound on the AT; the open summit is at about mile 1.3 (Appalachian Trail Conservancy)

events.note: 48-foot steel tower reported in an October 1929 Harrisonburg Daily News item, quoted by Forest Lookouts; the history gives 1929
USGS placed benchmarks; main station mark under the center of the tower
USGS 1958 note: tower torn down, concrete footings still in place
USGS 1961 note says the tower was moved and gave new measurements; the history reads this as a new tower erected
Second tower removed; Register dates removal to circa 1980s, so 1980 is approximate (see corrections)
Former lookout cabin (Register) or fire wardens house at the base (history) rehabilitated as the Chestnut Knob AT shelter

corrections.why: The Register gives circa 1980s for the removal; it does not give 1980.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the former lookout cabin is the shelter; the willhite history says the former fire wardens house at the base of the tower is the shelter; the Conservancy calls it an old stone fire warden's cabin. The story reports the Register's account and the history's account.
The Register gives 4,401 ft (1,341 m); the willhite history gives 4,409 ft. Elevation is not used in the story.

notes_for_editor: Built year 1929 rests on the Harrisonburg item quoted by Forest Lookouts and on the willhite history. The Register has no Built field. Two searches found no staffing or fire sources, so none are included. The shelter's identity is disputed between sources. The 1961 new-tower reading is the history's interpretation of USGS notes. The Nutty Hiker post is undated and is cited only for old foundations. Brief's 1980 removal year is approximate; corrected in corrections.
